props.title: The songs people sing along to under their breath.
props.lede: The singer-songwriter book, pop and soul from the last sixty years, and the acoustic side of classic rock: Tom Petty, Bill Withers, the Beatles ballads. The voice sings the song and the guitar carries the rest of the record.

props.html: The ballads play while people eat, and the songs with a pulse come out once people are standing. The whole covers list is on the repertoire page, and one learned song of your choosing comes with every booking, which for a wedding is usually the first dance or the processional.

props.title: Any of our singers, or one by name.

rows.text: One of the working singers who play this size, matched to your date and your crowd. Book it when the sound and the date matter more than the name.

A smoky voice and a guitar played with a funk guitarist’s right hand. He plays blues and classic rock, solo for welcome drinks and dinner and up to a four piece when the night wants a floor, with his own footage on his page.

A songwriter with his own catalog, folk and Americana on voice and acoustic guitar, who plays covers beside his own songs when the hour wants them. Solo for a ceremony, a cocktail hour or a dinner where people listen, and up to a four piece with his band, with his own footage on his page.

A singer-songwriter who builds familiar songs from the ground up with live looping, fronting a duo that grows to a quartet on one contract. It’s the booking when the hour should be one voice and the night should end on a dance floor.

props.html: If you want instrumental guitar with no voice, jazz standards and Spanish-tinged sets, that’s the solo guitarist. The same voice and guitar with a second musician is the acoustic duo, which is the size for a crowd past a hundred.

items.q: Is one singer with a guitar enough for a cocktail hour?
items.a: For most cocktail hours and patios, yes. One voice and a guitar sound like live music from across a terrace and stay under the conversation. Above about a hundred guests spread across a ballroom, the acoustic duo adds a second musician to fill the space.

About the level of two guests talking who have just met. People at the next table can hear the words and keep talking at their own level. One musician sets the level to the space, and a voice and a guitar stay there all night.

items.q: Can a singer and guitarist play a wedding ceremony and the cocktail hour?
items.a: Yes, and it's a common booking: an instrumental prelude and processional, then the same musician sings the cocktail hour on the terrace. The small sound system runs the officiant's microphone too, so the ceremony and the hour are one setup and one contract.
Sets run 45 to 60 minutes with music through the breaks, for a single hour or from arrival through dinner. If the night runs long, another half hour is easy to add on the night.

items.q: How is this different from the solo guitarist?
items.a: The voice. The solo guitarist is instrumental: jazz standards and Spanish-tinged sets that sit under a dinner. The singer and guitarist sings the songs out front, for the hours where guests want to hear a voice and know the words.

Yes, and patios and lawns are its regular work. It needs a covered, level and dry spot with power run to it, and we agree a plan for moving indoors with you ahead of time, because Colorado evenings cool fast and a guitar and a voice both slow down in the cold.
